question: Should OpenClaw accept `includeFamily` as the public model-facing way for `chat.history` and `sessions_history` to read bounded reset-family transcript ancestors, with `includeFamily` plus `offset` rejected?
rationale: The patch appears mechanically sound, but deciding whether agents/tools may opt into archived reset-family transcript visibility is a product and security-boundary choice that automation should not settle.

options.title: Accept bounded includeFamily
options.body: Merge the current contract after maintainer review, treating header-checked reset-family transcript visibility as the supported opt-in model/tool behavior.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require the branch to limit the new behavior to a different API shape or non-model surface if maintainers do not want this exposed through `sessions_history`.

options.title: Pause for archive-history design
options.body: Keep or close this PR in favor of a broader archived-history/session-recovery design if `includeFamily` is not the desired public contract.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded includeFamily
recommendation.body: Merge the current contract after maintainer review, treating header-checked reset-family transcript visibility as the supported opt-in model/tool behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion directly asks jalehman to review the API/session-history boundary, which is the unresolved decision.
